# communication-bridge.scud

## 1. Module Overview & System Context
The **communication-bridge** module serves as the critical translation layer between the low-voltage Microcontroller (LV domain) and the high-voltage isolated daisy chain (HV domain) used for battery monitoring. 

**Primary Function:**
- Translates Host UART or SPI signals into differential isolated signals for the BQ79616/BQ79612 monitor ICs.
- Provides a "Wake-up" signal (INH) to activate the rest of the BMS stack.
- Reports system-level faults via the NFAULT line.

**External Interfaces:**
- **Host Interface:** Connects to the Microcontroller Module via UART/SPI.
- **Daisy Chain Interface:** Isolated differential pairs (COMHP/N, COMLP/N) connecting to the BMS Monitor Modules.
- **Power:** Consumes 12V (BAT) and 3.3V/5V (VIO) from the Low-Voltage Power Supply.

## 2. Architectural Deviations (Baseline vs. Target)
The design is based on the BQ79600-Q1 Evaluation Module (EVM) but optimized for the stackable-bms system.

**Removed components/blocks:**
- **Evaluation Headers:** All development-specific headers (J2, J4, J7, J8, J9, J10, J11, J12, J13) and test points (TP1-TP17) are removed to minimize footprint.
- **Redundant Isolation Options:** The EVM provides multiple isolation paths (Capacitor vs. Transformer). This design selects **Transformer Isolation** for superior common-mode rejection and robustness in a 400V system.
- **Selection Jumpers:** Hard-wired configuration for either UART or SPI (to be determined by MCU requirements; default to SPI as per System Boundary implies "UART/SPI").

**Added/Modified components/blocks:**
- **Connector Standardization:** Replaced EVM headers with the specific interface connectors defined in the Module Boundary Document.
- **Protection:** Enhanced ESD protection on the host interface pins (VIO domain).

## 3. Components Inventory
Based on the BQ79600-Q1 EVM and synthesized requirements:

| Component | RefDes (Baseline) | Value/Part Number | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| ASIC | U1 | BQ79600-Q1 | SPI/UART to Isolated Daisy Chain Bridge |
| Transformer | T1, T2 | HMU1228NL | Isolation Transformer for COM lines |
| Decoupling Cap | C1 | 100nF, 50V | BAT decoupling |
| Decoupling Cap | C2 | 470nF, 10V | CVDD decoupling |
| Decoupling Cap | C3 | 470nF, 10V | DVDD decoupling |
| Decoupling Cap | C4 | 0.1uF, 10V | VIO decoupling |
| Termination Res | R23, R33 | 51 Ohm | COML differential termination |
| Termination Res | R24, R34 | 51 Ohm | COMH differential termination |
| Bias Resistors | R27, R28, R29, R30 | 499 Ohm | COM line biasing resistors |
| Filter Caps | C9, C10, C11, C12 | 100pF | COM line common-mode filters |
| Protection Diode | D4, D5 | TVS | ESD protection for COM lines |
| Status LED | D2 | Green | CVDD Power Good indicator (Optional) |
| Status LED | D3 | Red | NFAULT indicator (Optional) |
| Current Limit | R5, R11 | 200 Ohm | LED current limiting resistors |
| INH Pull-up | R1 | 10 Ohm | BAT to INH series resistor |
| INH Circuit | D1 | 5.1V Zener | INH protection |

## 4. Connectivity & Signal Flow
- **Power Path:** 
    - 12V BAT supply enters P2.1, filtered by C1.
    - 3.3V/5V VIO supply enters P2.2, filtered by C4.
    - U1 regulates BAT down to **DVDD (1.8V)** for internal logic and **CVDD (5V)** for COM drivers.
- **Host Communication:**
    - MCU connects via P2.4-P2.8 (SCLK, nCS, MOSI, MISO, SPI_RDY).
    - Signal levels are referenced to VIO.
- **Daisy Chain Communication:**
    - U1 drives COMHP/N and COMLP/N.
    - These signals pass through **Transformers T1/T2** for galvanic isolation.
    - The isolated side connects to the BMS Monitor stack via P1.1 and P1.2.
- **Control & Status:**
    - **INH (P2.10):** High-voltage output to wake up the system PMIC.
    - **NFAULT (P2.9):** Open-drain output to MCU indicating a system-level fault.

## 5. Uncertainties, Assumptions & Confidence
- **Isolation Method:** I have assumed Transformer isolation (HMU1228NL) based on the "400V System level" requirement and standard BMS practices. 
- **Interface Selection:** The boundary doc mentions "UART / SPI". The EVM uses the `nUART/SPI` pin to select. I am assuming the MCU will use **SPI** for higher throughput (12MHz), but the hardware should support selecting either via a resistor strap.
- **CVDD LED:** The schematic shows D2 on CVDD. CVDD is only active when the chip is awake, making it a good "Link/Active" indicator.
- **Confidence:** High for core ASIC functionality; Medium for specific ESD/EMC component values as they depend on final PCB layout.

IN_PROGRESS
